fits.wls: prespecified weighted-log fit of ln[1 - 2P(n)], primary for the X-memory decision
fits.binomial: binomial maximum-likelihood refit of all round counts (App. stats)

per_placement.method: observed: inverse-variance mean over the five days, se widened by sqrt(chi2/nu) when chi2/nu > 1 (nu = 4); binomial sigmas are half-widths of the quasi-likelihood 68% profile intervals. observed_plain: plain mean over the five days, se = sd / sqrt(5). predicted: plain mean over the five days of the model's prediction (each job's measured f), fitted with the same estimator. ratio = observed_plain / predicted_mean, so both sides are averaged alike; its se carries the observed error only. Lambda is pooled from the daily ratios (inverse-variance). The t test is within one placement (nu = 4); there is no test across placements.

placements_compared.note: The difference between the placements is descriptive: on every day these were the only usable distance-5 placements, and they overlap.

prespecified.source: runs/combined.json (pooled_x), the prespecified code at v0.2.0
prespecified.note: The prespecified summary value, quoted in the paper's results and abstract; the rule treats the ten repetitions as independent, which they are not.

agreement_tests.source: docs/analysis/results/fits.json (agreement, agreement_tests); wls replicates runs/combined.json model

calibration_scatter_check_exploratory.label: exploratory; the added spread comes from the predictions only (calibrations and idle-test f)

selection_check (reported errors on the.what: chosen day's mean reported error / mean over the other four days, per patch; mean over the five days

tracking.what: placement 1, Lambda_X: its prediction barely depends on f, so the predicted day-to-day swing comes from the calibration alone

prejob.what: predictions stored before each job (prediction.json) at f = 0 and f = 1, fitted like the data. The observed eps are decoded with priors at the job's measured f.

table_one_convention.convention: every cell, observed and predicted: plain mean over the five days. Observed error sqrt(sum sigma_i^2) / 5, multiplied by sqrt(chi2/nu) when chi2/nu > 1, chi2 about the plain mean, nu = 4. sigma_i is each estimator's own sampling error: binomial, half the 68% quasi-likelihood profile interval; WL, the delta-method sigma as prespecified in X memory, and in Z memory, where that sigma is unreliable near P = 1/2 (see errors), the parametric-bootstrap sd of the WL estimator. Predicted: plain mean of the daily predictions fitted the same way, with their range and sigma_M = sqrt(sum sigma_M,i^2) / 5 from the agreement test's sigma_M of each day.

errors.what: ratios are bootstrap sd / quoted sigma: above 1, the quoted sigma is too small. Parametric bootstrap, 2,000 replicates per curve drawn from its binomial fit (fits.json).

window.note: WL tests refitted from results/fits_counts.json exactly as prespecified, f term from the frozen f = 0 and f = 1 predictions refitted in the same window. Binomial O/M: point estimates, both sides fitted alike; Student t interval over the ten repetitions.

selection.what: excess per round O - M in percentage points and the factor O/M, per patch (plain mean or geometric mean over the five days, t 4 dof). An equal additive excess gives a larger factor at the smaller eps, so only the additive scale and the fixed-against-reselected comparison speak to selection.

power.what: power of chi2 = sum z^2 > 18.31 against the same miss in every repetition, noncentral chi2 with 10 dof at each repetition's sigma = sqrt(sigma_O^2 + sigma_M^2)

provenance.inputs of power.json: the frozen f = 0 and f = 1 predictions (prediction.json) of all fifteen jobs; days 2-5's were made on their own days
provenance.assumes: f known exactly (no f term) and sigma_O at the predicted curves

calibration_scatter_test_power.what: the exploratory test's chi2 over ten repetitions, sigma'^2 = sigma^2 + (s_Q M)^2

counts.what: k(n) of N against the model's P(n) at the measured f; chi2 with the chip's and the simulator's binomial variance at the model's P plus sigma_f^2 g g^T, g = P(f = 1) - P(f = 0); 'none' leaves out the f term. Groups: sums over the five days, one job each

equivalence.what: Lambda_X, O - M. Equivalent within a margin when the 90% t interval lies inside it (two one-sided tests at 5%); certified margin: the larger end of that interval. Power: the chance of certifying the margin if the model were exactly right, five units, at the observed sd between them and at the stated errors alone

prespecified pool (WL, inverse variance.note: the ten repetitions as independent; the prediction's own error left out, as in the rule

pool.rule: Eq. (pool), run.py: weights w_i = 1 / sigma_O,i^2 over the ten pair-days (WL); error sqrt(max(1, chi2_0 / nu) / sum w), chi2_0 = sum w (Lambda_i - Lambda)^2, nu = 9; d = 5 worse if Lambda + t_{nu,0.95} se < 1, better if Lambda - t se > 1. The pooled prediction uses the same weights.

sigma_f.what: prespecified sigma_f = 1.25 s_f / sqrt(n), the standard error of a median from the spread of the job's n per-qubit f; idle_noise sigma_f = sd of the median over 2000 parametric redraws of the idle test (sensitivity.py); ratio = idle_noise / prespecified

per_qubit_fits_overdispersed.what: each qubit-job's line in run._fit_share (Eq. S5): weighted residual chi2 at the fitted f, dof = idle lengths kept - 2. Uniformity = run._uniformity's chi2/nu about the inverse-variance mean f, then with each qubit's sigma times sqrt(max(1, chi2/dof)), qubits with no dof unscaled. The prespecified tests use sigma_f = 1.25 s_f / sqrt(n), which does not involve these per-qubit sigmas.

windows.what: plain means over each pair's five days of Lambda_X, device and model (the prediction at the measured f), both curves fitted on the same window by the same fit (sensitivity.py). Systematic = half the range over the ten choices below; rounds 3-8 are left out because there the distance-5 P(n) is 0.38-0.51 throughout and Lambda_X mostly noise.

table_pairs.convention: plain means over the five days. Error sqrt(sum sigma_i^2) / 5, times sqrt(chi2_0 / 4) when chi2_0 / 4 > 1, chi2_0 = sum ((v_i - mean) / sigma_i)^2, for observations and predictions alike. Observed sigma_i: each fit's own (WL delta method in X memory and the WL bootstrap sd in Z memory, binomial profile), as effect_sizes.py. Predicted sigma_i: the test's sigma_M with the prespecified sigma_f (and, in X memory, with the noise-only sigma_f as a check). For pair 1's Lambda_X the widened prediction error is the calibration's change from day to day, not the uncertainty of one prediction.

power.what: the same miss in every pair-day (WL, the prespecified fit); sigma_i = sqrt(sigma_O^2 + sigma_M^2). One pair-day: P(|z| >= 2) at a Lambda_X miss of 0.06. A pair: noncentral chi2, 5 dof, bound 11.07. All ten: noncentral chi2, 10 dof, bound 18.31, noncentrality sum (miss / sigma_i)^2; and the miss found with 80% probability.

xy_variance_correction.what: old: Var(ln r) = (1 - r^2)/(N r^2) as prespecified (run.py:1059); new: delta method for separately sampled <X> and <Y>, Var(ln r) = [x^2(1-x^2)/N_X + y^2(1-y^2)/N_Y]/r^4 (with the (1+1/N) shot-noise factors).

downstream.source: results/idle_f_{compare,reanalysis,reanalysis_control,combined_fixed,combined_control}.json; control = unpatched rerun in the same environment

largest_observed_Lambda_X_change.note: observed values move because the decoder weights depend on f

heating_exploratory.what: Fractional change of each error rate from the start (t=0) to the end (t=1) of a job's shots; slope of the series-normalized rate against time. See heating.py docstring.

onset_line.note: two CZ counts only (relays 3, flags 8): the line joins the two roles' means

about.streak: flag or relay i fired in rounds t-1 and t (x_{i,t-1} = x_{i,t} = 1)
about.A: unit = (job, circuit, series, round t); groups streak (1,1), single (0,1), quiet (0,0); outcome = fraction of the patch's near (share a data qubit) or far stabilizer detectors firing in round t + lag; D = sum w (ybar1 - ybar0) / sum w, w = n1 n0 / (n1 + n0); model = same w, exact model probabilities; CIs over shots (linearized) and clustered by physical qubit
about.B: strata (job, circuit, patch); exposed = a streak on any flag or relay of the patch; Mantel-Haenszel RD (Sato) and RR (Greenland-Robins); count matched = strata also by the number K of flag and relay firings in the patch; failure_per_firing = within-stratum least-squares slope of the failure on K; model = the same on its sampled, decoded shots

readout_gap_P01_minus_P10_flags_relays.days: qubit-days with the split for the calibration in force (properties.py)

beta_gamma_dd_on_gamma_phi.what: OLS slope of ln Gamma_dd on ln Gamma_phi over physical qubits (per-qubit medians); 1 if one f fits every qubit, 0 if Gamma_dd ignores IBM's T2

per_qubit_f_decoding.basis: X (Z memory is unchanged in every job)

fit.model: Delta(l) = A r^l + C, l = 1..7 rounds, unweighted least squares on the mean over series
Delta(l) = A r^l + C, l = 1..7 rounds, unweighted least squares on the mean over series

error_scale.what: k multiplies every error channel of the model (idles: every decay rate); k_eps matches the device's eps per round, k_det the mean bulk stabilizer detection rate of the eight-round circuit. Geometric means; placement intervals Student t over the five days, 'all ten' DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp 95%.

dephasing_floor.what: Gamma_dd = f Gamma_phi (1/us), the idle test's dephasing beyond T1, against IBM's Gamma_phi: one multiple, a floor, or both. Phase flips per round over the decoupled idle of a data qubit (X memory as sent).

model_idle_error_per_round.what: the model's idle error of a data qubit per round over its decoupled wait, at the job's f; medians over each patch's data qubits, then their range over the twenty patch-jobs

input_resolution.what: binomial standard error of IBM's reported readout error (4096 shots per prepared state), relative to the error, over the qubits of every job's patches

timing.what: one round (the middle one) of the 3-round X-memory circuit of day 1's first job, from the compiled circuit as sent: what each qubit does, and when

prerun_figure3_rows.scenario: d = 3 on qubits of the d = 5 patch
weak parts of both patches at the chip median
